Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: It is at the origin of the zodiacal constellation _____
Enki.fact: It is at the origin of the zodiacal constellation Capricorn.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: It was associated with him since the _____ period
Enki.fact: It was associated with him since the Old Akkadian period. Since the Old Akkadian period he could also be depicted alongside his Lahmu servants, divinities represented as naked or kilted male figures with abundant facial hair and locks of hair on each side of their face.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: Ea was often depicted alongside his two faced vizier _____
Enki.fact: Ea was often depicted alongside his two faced vizier Isimud.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: It is attested in pictorial representations from the _____ period up until Hellenistic times, and might have been the precursor of the merman in Greek and Medieval European art and literature
Enki.fact: It is attested in pictorial representations from the Neo Sumerian period up until Hellenistic times, and might have been the precursor of the merman in Greek and Medieval European art and literature.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: A well known example is the seal of _____
Enki.fact: A well known example is the seal of Adda.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: The god rising from the mountain is most often interpreted as _____, and the armed goddess as Ishtar
Enki.fact: The god rising from the mountain is most often interpreted as Shamash, and the armed goddess as Ishtar.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Enki.fact: Another well attested example is a motif where a half-man, half-bird creature is presented before an enthroned Ea by one or two gods, one of which is generally Isimud.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: Pierre Amiet proposed that the scene on the _____ cylinder may represent the revelation of the forces of nature in early spring
Enki.fact: Pierre Amiet proposed that the scene on the Adda cylinder may represent the revelation of the forces of nature in early spring.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Enki.fact: According to one text, the name of the boat was "Ibex of the Abzû". Enki's association with the ibex dates to the second half of the third millennium.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: The little owl is called the bird of Ea in the _____
Enki.fact: The little owl is called the bird of Ea in the Bird Call Text.

Enki.fact: It has been remarked that Nammu and An do not appear together in Sumerian or Akkadian literature, and only a single inscription refers to them as a couple.

Enki.question: In this context, she was syncretized with _____
Enki.fact: In this context, she was syncretized with Damgalnuna. In tablet II of the god list An=Anum she is equated with Damgalnuna.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: In tablet II of the god list An=Anum she is equated with _____
Enki.fact: In this context, she was syncretized with Damgalnuna. In tablet II of the god list An=Anum she is equated with Damgalnuna.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: Ningikuga was also the name of the mother of _____
Enki.fact: Ningikuga was also the name of the mother of Ningal.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: According to _____, this name refers to a single deity, while they are treated as separate goddesses in Ningikuga's Reallexikon der Assyriologie entry by Cavigneaux and Krebernik

Enki.fact: In this period, Marduk was assimilated to Asalluhi, a god of incantations who was regarded as a son of Enki and Damgalnuna. The syncretism between Asalluhi and Marduk is documented at the earliest in a letter of the king of Larsa Sin-Iddinam, where he is called "Asalluhi, king of Babylon".

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: The syncretism between _____ and Marduk was not fully complete in the Old Babylonian period, however, and they could still be occasionally referred to as separate deities
Enki.fact: In this period, Marduk was assimilated to Asalluhi, a god of incantations who was regarded as a son of Enki and Damgalnuna. The syncretism between Asalluhi and Marduk is documented at the earliest in a letter of the king of Larsa Sin-Iddinam, where he is called "Asalluhi, king of Babylon".

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: With the rise of _____'s importance in the pantheon grew and he took over certain characteristics of his father, such as his function as organizer of the earth
Enki.fact: With the rise of Babylon Marduk's importance in the pantheon grew and he took over certain characteristics of his father, such as his function as organizer of the earth.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: She could appear alongside him in sumerian and bilingual incantation texts, together with _____ and Nammu
Enki.fact: She could appear alongside him in sumerian and bilingual incantation texts, together with Asalluhi and Nammu.

Enki.fact: The hymn further states that she was raised by Ninhursag.

Enki.fact: Enbilulu could be regarded as a son of Enki and Damgalnuna; in the myth Enlil and Ninlil he is instead the son of the eponymous deities. It has been proposed that in the context of this hymn Ninti is an alternative name of Damgalnuna.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Enki.fact: Ea is called the father of Dumuzi (Tammuz) in Old Babylonian incantations, though he does not play a role in the narratives about this god.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: In the god list An=Anum, Ea is assigned several sons aside from Marduk; Dumuzi-abzu, Barra, _____, Burnuntasa, Nera, and Kigulla
Enki.fact: In the god list An=Anum, Ea is assigned several sons aside from Marduk; Dumuzi-abzu, Barra, Barragula, Burnuntasa, Nera, and Kigulla.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: Kigulla also appears elsewhere as a goddess, the wife of Nita, equated with _____
Enki.fact: Kigulla also appears elsewhere as a goddess, the wife of Nita, equated with Ninurta.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Enki.fact: In the god list An=Anum, Ea is assigned several sons aside from Marduk; Dumuzi-abzu, Barra, Barragula, Burnuntasa, Nera, and Kigulla. Dumuzi-abzu was originally the name of a female deity from the region of Lagash who was not called Enki's child in older sources.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Enki.fact: Dumuzi-abzu was originally the name of a female deity from the region of Lagash who was not called Enki's child in older sources. She is otherwise twice called "the daughter of Abzu" in incantations, and in the Šurpu incantation series she appears near him.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Enki.fact: Their names are reinterpreted as word play on the Sumerian words referring to his body parts.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: In an incantation text, Ea fashions from clay several craftsmanship deities, among them Ninšar and _____
Enki.fact: In an incantation text, Ea fashions from clay several craftsmanship deities, among them Ninšar and Ninkurra.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: A later text refers to Kaḫegal and Igiḫegal as lahmu of _____ or the Abzû
Enki.fact: They are attested in this role since Old Babylonian times onwards, and appear in association with Enki and Eridu in incantations. A later text refers to Kaḫegal and Igiḫegal as lahmu of Eridu or the Abzû.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: Lahmu were a class of supernatural beings regarded as servants of Ea, and later of his son _____
Enki.fact: Lahmu were a class of supernatural beings regarded as servants of Ea, and later of his son Marduk.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: Certain texts number fifty _____ at Ea's service
Enki.fact: Lahmu were a class of supernatural beings regarded as servants of Ea, and later of his son Marduk. Certain texts number fifty Lahmu at Ea's service.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: They are described as servants of Ea in the Epic of Erra, and are called "the _____ of Eridu" in a text from the first millennium BCE known as the Twenty One Poultices
Enki.fact: The Seven Sages (apkallu) were fish-men creatures of the Abzû regarded as responsible for teaching mankind various aspects of human culture, in a Babylonian and Assyrian tradition dating to the late second and the first millennium BCE. They are described as servants of Ea in the Epic of Erra, and are called "the Seven Sages of Eridu" in a text from the first millennium BCE called the Twenty One Poultices.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: It is presumed that they are identical with the _____
Enki.fact: They are described as servants of Ea in the Epic of Erra, and are called "the Seven Sages of Eridu" in a text from the first millennium BCE called the Twenty One Poultices. Mesopotamian traditions around the Seven Sages were the source for the later Babyloniaca of the Babylonian priest Berossos, which relates that a hybrid fish-human creature named Oannes came out of the sea to teach the inhabitants of Babylonia various aspects of human culture, such as writing, temple building and sciences.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Enki.fact: A connection between Ea and the South Wind is documented in texts; Essarhadon refers to her as the breeze of this god, and in an Assyrian incantation she is called "the beloved of Ea".

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: In Elam, Ea was possibly also associated with _____ and the Dilmunite god Enzag
Enki.fact: In Elam, Ea was possibly also associated with Inshushinak and the Dilmunite god Enzag.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: At Ebla, the local form of Ea was associated with Zilašu, the local form of the _____ beer goddess Siris
Enki.fact: At Ebla, the local form of Ea was associated with Zilašu, the local form of the Mesopotamian beer goddess Siris.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: He was also connected with Rašap, an _____ god
Enki.fact: He was also connected with Rašap, an Underworld god.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Enki.fact: In a god list part of an Ugaritic ritual, Ea is identified with Kothar-wa-Khasis, like him a god associated with craftsmanship.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: Ea and his spouse _____ were connected with the Hurrian goddesses of fate, Hutena and Hutellura, or to their Hittite counterparts, the Gulses and the Mother-Goddess, in some lists
Enki.fact: Ea and his spouse Damgalnuna were connected with the Hurrian goddesses of fate, Hutena and Hutellura, or to their Hittite counterparts, the Gulses and the Mother-Goddess, in some lists.

Enki.fact: Comparisons have been sometimes made between Ea and the Greek Titan Prometheus in modern scholarship.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: Some scholars have argued that _____ was assimilated to Ea by the Greeks, and that he acquired his role as a culture hero as a result, though this view is not universally accepted
Enki.fact: Comparisons have been sometimes made between Ea and the Greek Titan Prometheus in modern scholarship. Some scholars have argued that Prometheus was assimilated to Ea by the Greeks, and that he acquired his role as a culture hero as a result, though this view is not universally accepted.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: In _____, a team of Italian archaeologists under the direction of Paolo Matthiae of the University of Rome La Sapienza performed a series of excavations of material from the third-millennium BCE city
Enki.fact: In 1964, a team of Italian archaeologists under the direction of Paolo Matthiae of the University of Rome La Sapienza performed a series of excavations of material from the third-millennium BCE city of Ebla.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: Much of the written material found in these digs was later translated by _____
Enki.fact: Much of the written material found in these digs was later translated by Giovanni Pettinato.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Enki.fact: In the nineteenth and early twenty century some scholars proposed that the Israelite god Ya[hweh] was derived from the Mesopotamian Ea, and these views are upheld by a minority of modern scholars.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Enki.fact: His main cult center was the city of Eridu, which was regarded as his home already in the sources of the Early Dynastic Period.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: Eridu was one of the oldest cities of _____
Enki.fact: Eridu was one of the oldest cities of Sumer. It could be referred to with the by name Eengura ("House of Sweet Waters") in Sumerian literature or cultic laments.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Enki.fact: It could be referred to with the by name Eengura ("House of Sweet Waters") in Sumerian literature or cultic laments.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Enki.question: It is already attested in the _____, and is mentioned in sumerian literature such as the lament for Eridu and the hymn to Haya as well as in the later syncretistic hymn to Nanaya
Enki.fact: It is already attested in the Temple Hymns, and is mentioned in sumerian literature such as the lament for Eridu and the hymn to Haya as well as in the later syncretistic hymn to Nanaya.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Enki.fact: In the territory of Lagash, it is presumed that he was worshipped in the numerous shrines bearing the name "Abzû" in the region. One of these shrines, the Abzû-banda ("Small Abzû") was built by Ur-Nanshe and plundered some generations later by Lugalzagesi in his invasion of Lagash.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Enki.fact: One of these shrines, the Abzû-banda ("Small Abzû") was built by Ur-Nanshe and plundered some generations later by Lugalzagesi in his invasion of Lagash.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Enki.fact: His association to the arts of incantation was reflected in his epithets mašmaš ilī, "Exorcist of the gods", and bēl išīputti ("Lord of the purification rites"). Ea could be called Ea-šarru in some Akkadian texts.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Enki.fact: In Ebla, the logogram den-ki was used to write the name of the local form of Ea, Hayya, in the pre-Sargonic period.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Enki.fact: In Ebla, the logogram den-ki was used to write the name of the local form of Ea, Hayya, in the pre-Sargonic period. A festival of Ea is attested in Ebla, which took place in the twelfth month.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Enki.fact: Its name was Egeštušudu ("House of Perfect Wisdom").

Enki.fact: Enkum (purification priests) and Ninkum (purification priestesses) were another class of cultic officials from Eridu in the service of Enki. Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Enki.fact: The myth Inanna and Shukaletuda mentions khôl mascara worn by the ishib of Eridu.

Enki.fact: Evidence from tablets dating to the first two centuries of the second millennium indicate that he was one of the deities most frequently invoked in Mariote personal names.

Enki.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Enki.fact: Some examples include Ea-malik, Nabi-Ea, Rama-Ea and Idlal-Ea.

Enki.fact: Ea's temple in Kisurra was built by Itur-Shamash.
